## Why This Is Asked
This question probes ability to translate privacy-preserving on-device analytics into a concrete financial plan, balancing engineering costs with business value.

- Cloud aggregation costs vs data minimization savings
- Regulatory, privacy, and compliance overheads
- Rollout strategy, telemetry, and risk indicators

## Code Example

```javascript
function computeBreakEven(arpu, costPerDevice, devices) {

}
```

- How would you validate DP parameters in production without degrading user experience?
- What metrics signal a need to adjust rollout pacing or revert features?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests advanced system design: on-device ML with privacy guarantees, explainability, OTA updates, and regulatory considerations. It requires balancing compute, energy, latency, and business value at scale.

## Key Concepts

- On-device inference footprints (memory, CPU, energy)
- Explainability overhead and latency implications
- OTA update strategy and bandwidth budgeting
- Drift detection, validation costs, and governance
- Privacy/compliance costs and risk management
- Break-even analysis and go/no-go criteria

## Code Example

```javascript
function shouldGoLive(costs, benefits) {
  // simplified NPV check for go/no-go decision
  const npv = benefits.discounted - costs.discounted;
  return npv > 0;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- What drift detectors and validation experiments would you run offline and online?
- How would you audit privacy/compliance across OTA updates and data minimization?

## Why This Is Asked

- FP/FN UX trade-offs and calibration
- Privacy, telemetry, and compliance costs
- Break-even horizon and go/no-go criteria
- Model update cadence and maintenance

## Code Example
```javascript
// rough CBA scaffold
function cba(months, costs, savings){
  let payback = Math.ceil(months * (costs - savings));
  return {payback};
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate false positives in production?
- How would regional privacy rules alter the model and costs?
